title: Regional Capacity Matrix and Shift Handoff Handbook
author: Priya Malhotra
body:
Summary

This handbook documents the canonical regional capacity matrix, live capacity checks to run at shift start, and a compact on-call handoff checklist for the Platform team. It is intended for engineers taking regional shifts, SREs coordinating cross-region failovers, and managers planning capacity commits.

Why this exists

- Reduce ambiguity during handoff between shifts and regions.
- Provide a single authoritative mapping of which services, SKUs, and node pools carry production traffic per region.
- Standardize the capacity-check routine so that capacity regressions are detected before customer impact.

Scope and audience

- Scope: Redwood Inference production regions (us-west-2, us-east-1, eu-west-1, ap-southeast-1) and related dedicated pools.
- Audience: eng-platform oncall, eng-sre, infra-planners, and release engineers.

Table: Regional capacity matrix (snapshot fields)

Columns: Region | Primary GPU SKU | Dedicated pools | Typical sustained QPS | Planned headroom (%) | Autoscale min/max nodes | Critical services on pool

- us-west-2 | p4d.24xlarge | rdw-dedicated-wus | 18k tokens/s | 35% | 6 / 36 | serving-runtime, router, kv-cache
- us-east-1 | a100-80gb | rdw-dedicated-eus | 22k tokens/s | 30% | 8 / 48 | serving-runtime, auth, metrics-ingest
- eu-west-1 | a10x | rdw-dedicated-eu | 9k tokens/s | 40% | 4 / 24 | serving-runtime, routing, telemetry
- ap-southeast-1 | a100-40gb | rdw-dedicated-ap | 4k tokens/s | 45% | 2 / 12 | serving-runtime, cache-proxy

Note: This table is a live configuration — for exact current numbers consult the "capacity-matrix" sheet (link internal: /sheets/capacity-matrix).

Shift start checklist (6–8 items, run within first 15 minutes)

1. Pull the live capacity snapshot: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://platform-api.internal/v1/capacity/regions/current
2. Verify PG (primary GPU) availability: kubectl get node -l pool=primary -o wide --context ${REGION_CTX}
3. Check autoscale throttle events: kubectl logs deployment/autoscaler -n infra --since=1h | grep "throttle"
4. Confirm key SLOs are green for the past 15m: visit Grafana -> Platform SLOs -> Regional Overview or use the API: curl https://grafana.internal/api/metrics?query=slo_region_status&range=15m
5. Validate KV cache hit rate >= 65% for serving-runtime pools: query metrics endpoint (example provided below).
6. Confirm no active capacity incidents in PagerDuty (service: RDW-Platform-Capacity).

Quick commands

- Live capacity snapshot (JSON):
  curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://platform-api.internal/v1/capacity/regions/current | jq .

- Autoscaler events (last 2h):
  kubectl -n infra logs deployment/autoscaler --since=2h | tail -n 200

- KV cache hit rate (promql example):
  sum(rate(kv_cache_hits_total[5m])) / sum(rate(kv_cache_requests_total[5m])) * 100

SLOs referenced in handoff

- Serving p95 latency (inference path): 150ms target, alert at 220ms.
- Token generation availability: 99.95% monthly, severity-1 if <99.5% in last 1h.
- Control-plane API success rate: 99.9% daily.

Escalation and ownership matrix

- Capacity alerts (medium/high): Primary: oncall-eng-platform; Secondary: infra-autoscale oncall.
- Region-wide degradation: Primary: eng-sre-region-lead (pagerduty), Secondary: platform-ops-bot (Slack #platform-ops).
- Billing/quotas hit: Finance-ops notified, but immediate mitigation owned by eng-platform.

Actions on detection of capacity shortfall

1. If autoscale did not recover and node shortage persists > 5 minutes: trigger manual scale-up to restore minimum headroom:
   - Terraform scale example (apply a temporary emergency count):
     terraform apply -var 'region=${REGION}' -var 'pool=primary' -var 'desired_count=${NEW_COUNT}' -auto-approve
2. If a quota or cloud limit is blocking: open a support case with cloud provider using the incident template (link: /templates/cloud-support-case). Include exact request IDs and timestamps.
3. If model-serving latency increases but node counts are nominal: enable lighter quantized fallback model routing via routing policy (example CLI):
   rdwctl route set --region ${REGION} --service serving-runtime --fallback-model redwood/rlhf-quantized-v1
4. For persistent cross-region imbalance (> 30 minutes): engage regional failover playbook and re-route a percentage of traffic to neighboring region following the routing policy documented in /eng-platform/systems-and-services/service-lifecycle-orchestration-guidelines-2026.

Runbook snippet: rapid capacity triage (15 minute script)

- Step 0: identify affected region and service (from PagerDuty or Grafana alert).
- Step 1: gather telemetry (commands):
  - curl "https://platform-api.internal/v1/telemetry/region/${REGION}?window=15m" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" | jq .
  - kubectl -n serving-runtime get pods -l region=${REGION} -o=custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,CPU:.spec.containers[*].resources.requests.cpu,RESTARTS:.status.containerStatuses[*].restartCount
- Step 2: check scaling logs and recent node events.
- Step 3: if restart storms or OOMs are present, scale down concurrency and set temporary PDB relaxations:
  kubectl patch deployment serving-runtime -n ${NAMESPACE} -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"srv","env":[{"name":"MAX_CONCURRENCY","value":"4"}]}]}}}}'

Post-incident checklist (to run once immediate customer impact is resolved)

- Create postmortem stub within 24 hours under eng-platform/postmortems/. Include: timeline, root cause, contributing factors, mitigations, and owner for long-term fix.
- Metric snapshot: attach pre/post SLO graphs and capacity matrix diff.
- Follow-up actions: schedule a runbook update task and capacity plan in next weekly platform roadmap sync.

Capacity planning guardrails (policy bullets)

- Minimum headroom must be 30% for all production regions unless a documented business exemption is approved by the Platform leadership.
- No more than 20% of capacity should be assigned to experimental/ephemeral pools during a major release.
- All dedicated pools must expose a health endpoint: /healthz/capacity and return JSON {"allocatable_tokens_per_s": <int>, "node_count": <int>}.

Operational play examples

- Planned maintenance: bring pool to maintenance mode via rdwctl: rdwctl pool maintenance --pool rdw-dedicated-eu --start 2025-11-15T01:00Z --duration 2h --notify="#platform-ops"
- Rolling upgrade of compute nodes: follow the safe concurrency bump pattern (upgrade 10% of nodes, wait 10m, verify SLOs).

Handoff format example (to paste into PagerDuty or shift notes)

- Shift start: 2025-11-07 08:00 UTC
- Region(s) covered: eu-west-1
- Key observations: KV hit-rate 72%, autoscaler executed 2 scale-ups in last hour, serving p95 = 130ms.
- Active incidents: none
- Tasks in flight: terraform change #4321 pending approval
- Follow-ups: confirm quarantined node replacement during next quiet window.

Appendix: Useful links and references

- Capacity matrix (live): /sheets/capacity-matrix
- Routing policy doc: /eng-platform/systems-and-services/service-lifecycle-orchestration-guidelines-2026
- Incident template: /templates/incident-postmortem
- Grafana: https://grafana.internal/d/rdw-platform/regions
- PagerDuty: https://pagerduty.redwood.com/services/RDW-Platform-Capacity

Revision history

- 2024-02-12: Initial draft (Priya).
- 2024-06-03: Added KV hit-rate threshold and autoscale checklist (reviewers: Liam).
- 2025-11-07: Updated region SKUs and oncall handoff template; clarified Terraform emergency scaling guidance (reviewers: Daria, Marco).
